a: Used before a singular countable noun to refer to one person or thing without identifying which.
an: The form of the indefinite article used before a word beginning with a vowel sound.
the: Used before a noun to identify a particular person or thing already known, mentioned, or understood.
and: Connects words, phrases, or clauses to express addition or combination.
or: Connects alternatives or introduces another way to express something.
but: Connects a statement with a contrasting idea or exception.
if: Introduces a condition on which something depends.
although: Introduces a fact that contrasts with the main statement.
unless: Introduces the only condition that would prevent the main statement from being true.
whether: Introduces a choice between possibilities, or a question about which possibility is true.
while: Introduces something happening at the same time, or a contrasting fact.
as: Introduces a role, comparison, manner, reason, or simultaneous event, according to the construction.
at: Identifies a particular place, time, point, or target.
by: Identifies an agent or means, a nearby position, or a deadline.
for: Introduces a purpose, recipient, benefit, reason, or period of time.
from: Identifies the starting point, origin, or source of something.
in: Expresses location within something or within a period of time.
into: Expresses movement towards the inside of something, or a change of state.
of: Connects a noun with its possessor, source, contents, material, or a larger whole.
on: Expresses contact with a surface, a topic, or a particular day or date.
onto: Expresses movement to a position on a surface.
to: Introduces a destination, recipient, limit, or the base form of a verb.
with: Expresses accompaniment, possession of a feature, or the instrument used.
without: Expresses the absence of someone or something.
within: Expresses a position inside a boundary or before the end of a period.
about: Introduces the subject of a statement or thought, or an approximate quantity.
above: Expresses a position higher than something, or a level beyond a stated amount.
after: Expresses a later time or a position following something.
against: Expresses opposition, contact with a surface, or comparison with a standard.
among: Expresses being included in, surrounded by, or shared across a group.
before: Expresses an earlier time or a position in front of something.
behind: Expresses a position at the back of something or less progress than another.
below: Expresses a position lower than something or less than a stated level.
beside: Expresses a position next to someone or something.
between: Expresses a position, relationship, or choice connecting distinct people or things.
beyond: Expresses a position farther away than something, or outside a stated limit.
during: Expresses that something happens within the course of a period or event.
despite: Introduces a circumstance that does not prevent something from happening.
through: Expresses movement from one side to another, or completion of a process or period.
throughout: Expresses presence in every part of a place or during the whole of a period.
towards: Expresses direction, an attitude to someone, or progress towards a goal.
until: Identifies the time up to which an action or state continues.
upon: A formal alternative to on, often expressing contact or the moment something happens.
than: Introduces the second part of a comparison.
I: Refers to the person speaking or writing, as the subject of a clause.
you: Refers to the person or people being addressed, or to people in general.
he: Refers to a male person already identified, as the subject of a clause.
she: Refers to a female person already identified, as the subject of a clause.
it: Refers to an identified thing, animal, situation, or idea; also supplies a grammatical subject for weather, time, and similar expressions.
we: Refers to the speaker or writer together with one or more other people, as the subject of a clause.
they: Refers to people or things already identified, or to a person whose gender is unspecified or who uses this pronoun.
me: The object form of I, referring to the person speaking or writing.
him: The object form of he, referring to a male person already identified.
her: The object form of she; before a noun, indicates that something belongs to or is associated with a female person.
us: The object form of we, referring to the speaker or writer and one or more other people.
them: The object form of they, referring to identified people or things, or to a person who uses this pronoun.
my: Indicates that something belongs to or is associated with the speaker or writer.
your: Indicates that something belongs to or is associated with the person or people addressed.
his: Indicates that something belongs to or is associated with a male person already identified.
its: Indicates that something belongs to or is associated with an identified thing or animal.
our: Indicates that something belongs to or is associated with the speaker or writer and others.
their: Indicates that something belongs to or is associated with people or things referred to as they.
this: Identifies a particular nearby person, thing, or idea, or one currently being discussed.
that: Identifies a particular person, thing, or idea; also introduces a subordinate clause or a defining relative clause.
these: The plural of this, identifying particular nearby people or things.
those: The plural of that, identifying particular people or things treated as farther away.
who: Asks about a person's identity or introduces a relative clause referring to a person.
whom: The object form of who, especially in formal language or after a preposition.
whose: Asks or states which person or thing something belongs to.
which: Asks or states the particular member of an identified set.
what: Asks about, or refers to, the identity or nature of something.
where: Asks about a place or introduces a clause identifying a place or situation.
when: Asks about a time or introduces a clause identifying a time.
why: Asks for the reason for something.
how: Asks about the manner, condition, degree, or means of something.
be: Forms continuous verb constructions with an -ing form and passive constructions with a past participle.
am: The first-person singular present-tense form of be, used with I.
is: The third-person singular present-tense form of be.
are: The present-tense form of be used with you, we, they, and plural subjects.
was: The past-tense form of be used with I and usually with singular third-person subjects.
were: The past-tense form of be used with you and plural subjects; also used in certain hypothetical constructions.
have: Combines with a past participle to form perfect verb constructions.
has: The third-person singular present-tense form of have.
had: The past tense and past participle of have.
do: Forms questions, negatives, and emphatic statements with a base-form verb when another auxiliary is not used.
does: The third-person singular present-tense form of do.
can: Expresses ability, permission, or a possibility arising from circumstances.
could: Expresses past ability, a possible situation, or a polite request.
might: Expresses a possibility, often with greater uncertainty or tentativeness.
must: Expresses necessity, obligation, or a conclusion considered very likely.
shall: Expresses a future action, an offer or suggestion with I or we, or a formal requirement.
should: Expresses advice, expectation, or something considered right or desirable.
will: Expresses a future action, willingness, a promise, or a characteristic tendency.
would: Expresses a hypothetical result, a past habit, or a polite request.
not: Makes a word, phrase, or clause negative.
n't: A contracted form of not attached to an auxiliary or modal verb.
can't: A contracted form of cannot: is not able to, or is not permitted to.
cannot: The negative form of can, expressing inability or lack of permission.
don't: A contracted form of do not.
doesn't: A contracted form of does not.
didn't: A contracted form of did not.
won't: A contracted form of will not.
isn't: A contracted form of is not.
aren't: A contracted form of are not.
it's: A contracted form of it is or it has; unlike its, it does not mark possession.
